title: Debiasing Personal Identities in Toxicity Classification
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures unintended bias in toxicity classification against specific religious subgroups. It uses metrics like Subgroup AUC, BPSN AUC, and BNSP AUC to evaluate a model's ability to distinguish toxic from non-toxic comments within these subgroups without being unfairly biased.
base_benchmarks: Nuanced Metrics for Measuring Unintended Bias
findings: The paper found that a BERT model trained on a dataset that included identity-targeted comments (the 'Mixed Model') performed better at classifying toxic comments targeting religious subgroups (Christian, Jewish, Muslim) than a model trained on a dataset where such comments were removed (the 'Naive Model'). While overall AUCs were similar, the Mixed Model showed higher Subgroup AUCs, indicating that exposure to biased data during training is necessary to accurately identify toxicity directed at specific subgroups.
references: Borkan et al, "Nuanced Metrics for Measuring Unintended Bias with Real Data for Text Classifi-cation.", Jigsaw, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1903.04561v2.pdf
